text: Foundation Model Security for the Enterprise
Sanchit Alekh  ·  Google Cloud  ·  August 27, 2026
Agenda
The threat surface — models, weights, agents
What the frontier labs actually do
Prompt injection and the agentic reality check
Defence in depth, and a 90-day plan
Why now
Three shifts turned foundation-model risk into a board-level issue.
Frontier labs now gate autonomous AI R&D, cyber uplift and biological uplift as explicit capability thresholds.
EU AI Act GPAI obligations apply from 2 August 2025; systemic-risk fines reach €15M or 3% of turnover from 2026.
MCP tool poisoning and indirect injection moved from proofs of concept to CVEs, including CVE-2025-6514.
OWASP, NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS and ISO/IEC 42001 now give auditors a concrete yardstick.
The threat surface has four distinct layers
Model layer
Weights and training
RAND catalogues 38 attack vectors and 167 controls across five security levels, SL1 to SL5.
Application layer
Prompt and response
Instruction and data share one channel, so retrieved content can redirect the model's objective.
Agent layer
Tools and identity
Once a model can call tools, a content compromise becomes an action compromise under its own identity.
All three frontier labs refreshed their safety frameworks in 2025 — and they converge.
Responsible Scaling Policy. AI Safety Levels bind security and deployment controls to capability. Claude Opus 4 shipped under ASL-3.
Preparedness Framework v2. Tracked categories scored against High and Critical thresholds, with deployment gated on mitigations.
Frontier Safety Framework v3. Critical Capability Levels now cover CBRN, cyber, ML R&D uplift, harmful manipulation and misalignment.
Evaluate for dangerous capability, define a threshold, pre-commit to mitigations, re-evaluate as capability scales.
Indirect prompt injection has no complete defence today. Every published mitigation reduces attack success without eliminating it.
Containment over prevention: assume the agent will execute adversarial instructions, and design for blast radius.
Defence in depth
Tier the controls, not the policy. A single blanket standard either blocks low-risk adoption or under-protects autonomous agents.
Mapping controls to the Google Cloud estate
CONTROL MAP

Model Armor screens prompts, responses and agent interactions. Security Command Center AI Protection discovers AI assets and detects posture risk. Sensitive Data Protection redacts PII. VPC Service Controls and CMEK contain blast radius and protect data at rest.
Deployment tiers T1–T4
Controls scale with autonomy
Chat → RAG → tool-using agent → multi-agent autonomy
MATURITY
From perpetual pilot to governed production. Maturity is measured by containment and evaluation, not by model choice.
A 90-day plan
Days 0–30 — Inventory AI assets and shadow AI; classify by deployment tier
Days 30–60 — Enforce non-human identity and per-tool authorisation on agents
Days 60–90 — Stand up the evaluation harness and red-team the top three workflows
Ongoing — Map evidence to EU AI Act and ISO/IEC 42001 obligations
